claims.predicate: Capacity revenue MUST be recognized as the stand-ready obligation is satisfied over the delivery year.
The commencement date MUST be the date the asset is made available for use by the counterparty.
Amounts collected on behalf of another party MUST be presented net rather than gross.
Distinct performance obligations in the offtake agreement MUST be identified and the transaction price allocated among them.
The responsible entity MUST maintain a current inventory of cyber assets within the electronic security perimeter.
Device certificates used for control-path authentication MUST be rotated before expiry without interrupting the reliability function.
All external routable connectivity to control systems MUST traverse a defined electronic access point.
Evidence of compliance MUST be retained for the audit period specified by the applicable measure.
Inbound and outbound control traffic at the electronic access point MUST be subject to malicious-communications detection.
Security patches for applicable cyber assets MUST be assessed within the prescribed period of release.
Continuous discharge MUST NOT exceed 78 MW when ambient temperature is at or above 45 degrees Celsius, per the ambient derate curve.
Permitted capacity MUST NOT exceed 100 MW at the point of interconnection.
The applicant SHOULD give preference to local suppliers and labour where commercially reasonable.
Sound pressure level at the nearest property line MUST NOT exceed 45 dBA as a one-hour average during night hours.
Equipment MUST be set back from the property line by the distance stated in the permit condition.
Maximum cell temperature MUST NOT exceed the limit established in the accepted analysis.
Each enclosure MUST provide deflagration venting sized per the accepted analysis.
Sustained discharge over a four-hour window MUST NOT exceed 70 MW, being the usable energy admitted by the 85/15 percent state-of-charge window divided by four hours.
The accepted state-of-charge and temperature conditions MUST NOT be overridden by any operational, economic, or grid-emergency instruction.
BMS-reported state of charge MUST NOT exceed 85 percent when ambient temperature is at or above 40 degrees Celsius.
BMS-reported state of charge MUST NOT fall below 15 percent, reserving energy for thermal management and emergency response.
An access pathway MUST be maintained to each enclosure for emergency response.
Enclosures MUST be separated by the minimum distance established by the applicable large-scale fire test, or by a listed barrier.
The stored energy of a single group MUST NOT exceed the applicable maximum without additional protection measures.
The insured MUST operate in compliance with the accepted hazard mitigation analysis as a condition of coverage.
The insured MUST notify the insurer of any sustained derate attributable to thermal or degradation causes.
State of charge MUST NOT exceed the limit accepted in the hazard mitigation analysis; exceedance is a breach of a policy condition.
Cycle counting for warranty purposes MUST use the equivalent-full-cycle definition, being throughput divided by nameplate energy.
The battery management system MUST run the manufacturer's current released firmware revision to maintain warranty coverage.
Given 80 percent of the annual throughput budget consumed at 61 percent of the contract year, sustained discharge over a four-hour window MUST NOT exceed 55 MW for the remainder of the year.
Cumulative annual energy throughput MUST NOT exceed the warranted budget for the contract year, on pain of voiding cell coverage.
During a declared system emergency the resource MUST follow the operator's instruction without curtailment for local economic or contractual reasons.
A storage resource MUST submit upper and lower energy-limit parameters consistent with its physical capability for each market interval.
A dispatchable resource MUST follow the operator's active-power setpoint within the prescribed response window.
Derates and outages MUST be reported through the operator's outage system before the affected interval.
A storage resource MAY elect an energy-management sub-mode that restricts its offered range in exchange for relaxed state-of-charge management obligations.
A storage resource MUST telemeter state of charge to the market operator at the prescribed scan rate.
Station auxiliary load MUST be netted against delivered energy at the metering point rather than settled separately.
Accredited capacity MUST be determined by the operator's accreditation model and MUST NOT be assumed equal to nameplate rating.
A storage resource seeking a full capacity commitment MUST demonstrate four continuous hours of discharge at its committed level.
During a performance-assessment interval the resource MUST deliver at least its committed capacity obligation of 82 MW for four continuous hours.
A committed resource MUST offer its full committed capacity into the day-ahead market in every eligible hour.
Shortfall against the committed obligation MUST be assessed a non-performance charge per MWh not delivered.
Revenue metering MUST meet the accuracy class specified for wholesale settlement.
Metered quantities MUST be loss-compensated to the contractual delivery point using the stated transformer loss factor.
Settlement quantities MUST be read at the revenue metering point on the low side of the main power transformer.
Interval metered energy MUST be reconciled against control-path telemetry, with metered values governing on disagreement.
The inverter MUST cease to energize the area network upon loss of the utility source.
A DER MUST NOT execute a retail-program control and a wholesale dispatch instruction for the same interval.
The inverter MUST ride through voltage and frequency excursions within the specified envelope rather than tripping.
Energy MUST be delivered at the contractual delivery point on the high side of the main power transformer.
Net injection at the point of interconnection MUST NOT exceed 100 MW.
Certified protection settings MUST NOT be altered without written approval of the transmission provider.
The facility MUST maintain reactive capability across the specified power-factor range at the point of interconnection.
Control-signal round-trip latency MUST NOT exceed 150 milliseconds, so that the four-second regulation obligation is met with margin.
Any active derate MUST be published to the market operator's outage system and to the asset manager within the reporting window.
The plant MUST be capable of supporting an intentional island for the site's critical loads on loss of the utility source.
The plant controller MUST arbitrate between wholesale dispatch and retail-program signals by a documented, deterministic priority.
The controller MUST clamp any received setpoint to the intersection of all active operating limits before acting on it.
The default control mode SHOULD remain in effect whenever no higher-priority schedule or event is active.
Claimed eligible cost MUST be substantiated by supplier certifications and procurement records.
To qualify for the domestic-content bonus, domestic content MUST be at least the applicable percentage of eligible project cost.
The facility MUST be placed in service in the taxable year for which the credit is claimed.
The facility MUST NOT be disposed of or cease to be qualifying property during the recapture period.

Every sponsor is treated as granted to the SAVVI WorkOS Organization with the full permission set (`sponsor:edit`, `sponsor:analytics`, `deploy:nonproduction`, `deploy:production`, plus future). Owning-org visibility does not constrain SAVVI (§4.5.1).
Within SAVVI, auto-granted sponsors follow §4.5 (arrive `public`, AUTH-39); SAVVI admins may tighten visibility and use SAVVI teams normally.
The system grant is not revocable by other orgs; grant listings show it as a system grant (AUTH-34).
System grant is a **rule, not rows** in the effective-permission function (AUTH-14, §4.11).
Platform create, import, and the in-app Impersonate entry point require **SAVVI admin**.
Impersonation capability is WorkOS-only (environment opt-in + dashboard seats). The in-app entry point is a UX signal for SAVVI admins only.
Impersonation sessions surface via `impersonator` / `act` claim (in-app banner) and WorkOS `session.created` audit events.
SAVVI WorkOS Organization requires MFA.
The local dev login (`/dev/login`) bypasses WorkOS and is gated by the `DEV_AUTH_ENABLED` runtime flag. It must never be enabled outside local development.
`sponsor:edit` never implies deploy. Public baseline never includes `deploy:*` (AUTH-41).
`deploy:production` and `deploy:nonproduction` are distinct. Production envs require `deploy:production`; non-production accepts either.
`deploy:*` comes only from team roles (§2.5) and/or §4.6 grants.
Deploy sponsor X to environment E iff effective permission on X includes `sponsor:edit` and the matching `deploy:*`, and E is on X's platform and visible to the user (AUTH-59).

**Platform visibility**: a platform is visible to its owning org (as owner) and — as non-owner viewer — to orgs holding a §4.6 grant on any of its sponsors or a reseller agreement for it. SAVVI sees all platforms as owner. **Environment visibility** follows platform visibility.

Platform create requires **SAVVI admin** (AUTH-27). Platform attribute edits and environment management (create/edit/delete) are reserved to the platform-owning organization (SAVVI acts as owner everywhere). Platform deletion requires SAVVI admin. An environment is **production** iff its stage is `production` (AUTH-25).

Who may grant a sponsor to another WorkOS Organization: platform users with `sponsor:edit`, org admins, SAVVI staff (AUTH-20), and **reseller admins** for stamped sponsors (AUTH-51, no escalation). Each grant carries an explicit permission set from §2.4; orthogonal permissions (`sponsor:analytics`, `deploy:*`) only when listed. At most one grant exists per (sponsor, recipient org); granting again updates that grant's permission set (AUTH-32).

In the recipient org, team roles and visibility baselines apply **intersected** with the grant (check-time, §4.11). An orthogonal permission carried by a grant is therefore effective only where the derived side also confers it: `sponsor:analytics` via a team role or a public baseline listing it (AUTH-41), `deploy:*` via team roles only (AUTH-26). Example — grant `{sponsor:view}`: | Broker team role | Role would confer | Effective on Acme | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `implementor` | `sponsor:edit`, `sponsor:analytics`, `deploy:nonproduction` | `sponsor:view` (limited by grant; analytics/deploy not granted) | | `reporter` | `sponsor:report` | `sponsor:report` |
Grants and their permission sets are editable/revocable by the same parties as AUTH-30. Revocation takes effect on the next check; recipient team assignments become inert (AUTH-17).

Grants are non-transferable except stamped reseller orgs (AUTH-50/51), which extend grants to collaborating orgs (brokers, the sponsor's own org) **on behalf of the platform**, capped **at issue time** to the reseller's own granted set (no escalation, including edits to its own grant). Once issued, such grants are ordinary platform grants — AUTH-30/32 parties edit or revoke them; creator provenance is `sponsor_grants.created_by_id`. Narrowing the reseller's own grant later does not retroactively narrow grants it already issued.

Platform-owning org, stamped reseller org, and recipient org can each list grants they respectively own or hold. Listing authority mirrors management (AUTH-30) on the owning side; on the recipient side, org admins may list grants held by their org.
Membership/user deletion removes corresponding `team_memberships`. Org lifecycle webhooks only maintain the `organizations` mirror.
Authorization-data changes are recorded in `authz_audit_log`. The log is append-only; reading it is reserved to SAVVI admins.

Every organization kind (§2.1) may authenticate through SSO, email domain, or email invite. Each platform-owning org, reseller, broker, sponsor organization, and SAVVI is a distinct **WorkOS Organization**. WorkOS Organizations provide authentication (org-scoped sessions), SSO and other auth methods (domains, invitations, MFA where required — AUTH-54), and memberships with org-level roles such as `admin` (AUTH-53). Studio authorization is layered in the application database (§4.11); it is not WorkOS FGA. On the SAVVI organization, org `admin` also covers AUTH-27.

A user is a single identity (one account, one email) that may hold memberships in **any number of WorkOS Organizations**, each with its own org-level role. Multi-org membership is the exception, not the collaboration mechanism — cross-org access flows through grants (§4.6).
A user always acts in exactly **one active WorkOS Organization**. Authorization is evaluated for (user, active org); switching org re-derives roles, permissions, and visibility.
Each WorkOS Organization controls its own authentication policy. Access shared across organizations (§4.6) never subjects a user to another organization's identity provider.

An **org admin** holds AuthKit `admin` on their active membership (JWT claim, §4.11). That claim gates team creation (AUTH-52), team management (AUTH-9), visibility (§4.5.1), grant management (AUTH-30), and private-sponsor visibility (AUTH-12). Shorthand roles (§2.3) are org admins of those organization kinds. Because the claim lives in the session JWT, org-role changes take effect when the token refreshes (login, org switch, session refresh) — not necessarily on the next request, unlike database-backed authorization (§4.11).

Effective permission on a sponsor = union(visibility baseline §4.5.1, team-role permissions §2.5) ∩ grant set (AUTH-31). The union takes the max tier and keeps any orthogonal permission (`sponsor:analytics`, `deploy:*`) either side confers. Platform-owning org and SAVVI (§4.8) use the full set as the grant cap. One pure function (§4.11) answers point checks, lists, search, and deploy (AUTH-49).
A user's sponsor list is their org's pool at effective permission per sponsor (excluding AUTH-12-hidden), filterable to "my teams" (AUTH-36). Broker orgs span granted platforms without org switching.
Downstream entities (plan years, documents, products, comments) inherit from the parent sponsor's permission, with two named exceptions: task-level visibility and task-comment attachments (§4.12).
Unauthorized access returns not-found (no existence oracle).
A **sponsor** is owned by exactly one **platform**. Sponsors are never shared across platforms.

Sponsors are created under a platform by users who may create on that platform: any user of the platform-owning organization, SAVVI staff (§4.8), and any user of an org with a **reseller agreement** for the platform (§4.7). There is no per-user create designation. Regardless of who creates it, the sponsor is owned by the platform (AUTH-3). At create time the creator chooses team assignment(s) and the creating org's visibility; after creation, only an **org admin** of that org may change visibility (AUTH-41).

Sponsor ownership is a **two-level hierarchy**. Primary owner: the platform (AUTH-3) / platform-owning organization. Optional subordinate stamp: exactly one **reseller org** (`sponsors.reseller_organization_id`) for reseller-created sponsors (AUTH-44). Ownership is independent of team assignments (AUTH-48).

The reseller stamp confers authority subordinate to the primary owner: - **Grant management** for the sponsor (§4.6), never beyond the reseller org's own granted set. - **Lifecycle management** (archive/offboard, etc.), subject to primary-owner override. - The primary owner may edit/revoke any grant and reassign or clear the stamp. - The stamp is not transferable by the reseller and does not by itself confer sponsor permissions — access still flows through the §4.6 grant and the reseller's own teams.

Sponsor attribute edits require effective `sponsor:edit` (AUTH-14). Sponsor **deletion** is reserved to users of the platform-owning organization and SAVVI staff, and removes downstream data. There is no sponsor archive state — retirement is modeled by archiving plan years (story 33). A stamped reseller's lifecycle authority (AUTH-51) covers archival/offboarding workflows, not deletion.

**Task templates** are platform-scoped, optionally audienced to a reseller. Managing them (create/edit/delete) requires SAVVI staff or an org admin of the platform-owning organization. Instantiating a template follows normal task-creation rules (effective `sponsor:edit` on the target sponsor), and the template's platform/reseller audience must match the sponsor.

A **platform admin** or **SAVVI admin** may establish a **reseller agreement** between a platform and another WorkOS Organization. **Platform admins** may add a reseller **only by name and domain** (reuse the WorkOS Organization that owns the domain, or create and mirror one); they must not be offered an organization picker that would disclose other platforms' reseller partners. **SAVVI admins** may add by selecting an existing mirrored organization **or** by name and domain. Webhooks never invent agreements. The agreement confers `sponsor:create` (AUTH-42) and specifies a platform-owned **book team** and default **grant permission set** (typically `{sponsor:edit}`). Platform admins see only their agreements; SAVVI admins may manage any platform's.

Reseller-created sponsors: stamp `reseller_organization_id` (AUTH-50/51), assign to the book team, and §4.6-grant to the reseller org (enters as `public`, AUTH-39). Immediate — no platform-owner approval. Platform admins may also create a sponsor and assign it to a reseller.

Book team stays platform-owned (AUTH-4, AUTH-6); reseller users are never members. Reseller access is via the grant only. Cross-org team isolation holds (§4.5.2): reseller users do not see platform teams; platform users do not see reseller teams.
Removing an agreement drops `sponsor:create` only; stamps, grants, book-team assignments, and the reseller organization remain.

Onboarding a sponsor's WorkOS Organization: grant its sponsor to it (§4.6, typically `{sponsor:edit}`), auto-provision a default team owned by that org with the sponsor assigned, and add sponsor-org users per the onboarding agreement.
Sponsor-org users follow the same team/grant rules as any other organization.

Tasks carry their own visibility (`public` default / `restricted` / `private`), orthogonal to sponsor access. A task's **participants** — assignee, delegate, and subscribers — always see it in full detail, even without any permission on its sponsor. Non-participants need `sponsor:view` on the parent sponsor and see: | Task visibility | Participant | `sponsor:view` non-participant | | ------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------ | | `public` (default) | full | full | | `restricted` | full | attributes only | | `private` | full | not-found (AUTH-17) | The attributes projection is an allowlist (title, type, status, priority, dates, assignment, hierarchy) — never description or comments. Full-detail access gates comments and related task operations.

Plan-year **documents** require `sponsor:view` via the parent sponsor (AUTH-16). Task-comment **attachments** are a distinct document kind and follow the visibility of the task whose comment carries them: full-detail access to that task is required; document rules never apply. S3 upload and download tokens are issued only after these same checks.
Team membership is admin-managed only (no self-service join). Roster presence is accountability, not the access gate for `public` sponsors (AUTH-35).
A **team** is owned by exactly one WorkOS Organization.
A sponsor may be assigned to any number of teams. Cross-org assignment requires a **sponsor grant** (§4.6).

Teams are created and deleted by **org admins** of the owning org. Team admins manage existing teams (AUTH-8) but do not create or delete them. Deleting a team drops its sponsor assignments; if it was the only team assigned to a `private` sponsor, that sponsor remains visible only to org admins (AUTH-12). A team may be left with no team admin; org admins (AUTH-9) remain its management path.
Team members are always users of the team's owning organization. No guest membership.
Teams are flat (no nesting).
Team `admin`s can rename the team, change its visibility, manage membership (all roles), and assign/unassign sponsors.
Org admins can do everything a team admin can on any team in their org, including private teams.

A user's **collaborating organizations** are: their own org, the platform-owning org and every grant-holding org of each sponsor in their org's pool, and SAVVI (AUTH-23). The user directory lists active members of collaborating orgs only (default scope) or own-org members only (team pickers, AUTH-6); an all-users scope is SAVVI-staff-only. The directory is never a vehicle to enumerate unrelated organizations' users.

Direct user lookup succeeds for SAVVI staff, for active members of a collaborating org, and for users referenced on an entity the viewer can already see (plan-year contact/implementor/broker, task assignee/delegate); otherwise not-found (AUTH-17).

The full organization catalog is browsable by **SAVVI staff** (including selecting existing orgs as resellers, AUTH-43) and by **org admins** of reseller orgs under agreement or holding stamped sponsors (grant recipient pickers). **Platform-owning org admins do not** receive the full catalog — they add resellers by name and domain only (AUTH-43) so other platforms' reseller partners are not disclosed. Everyone else sees only organizations they belong to.
`restricted`: org-wide `sponsor:report`; view/edit require a sufficient team role on an assigned team.

`private`: invisible (not-found) except to members of an assigned team (at their role's level), **org admins** of an org holding the sponsor in its pool (at that org's public baseline, still ∩ grant — AUTH-31), and SAVVI staff (§4.8).
Search covers the org's sponsor pool excluding AUTH-12-hidden sponsors; restricted surfaces at `sponsor:report`.
A `public` sponsor confers the org's public baseline on every org user (intersected with the grant for granted sponsors, AUTH-31).
Lists filterable to "my teams".
A public team's sponsor list is filtered by the viewer's own sponsor-visibility rights (AUTH-11/AUTH-12).

Granted sponsors enter the recipient org as `public`; recipient admins may tighten afterwards. Mind the combined default: with AUTH-41's default baseline, granting `{sponsor:edit}` immediately gives every user of the recipient org edit on the sponsor — grant narrowly or have the recipient tighten visibility when that is not intended.

Public baseline is org-level (`organizations.public_sponsor_permissions`); default `sponsor:edit`, may lower to `sponsor:view`, and may additionally include `sponsor:analytics`. Restricted baseline is always `sponsor:report`. Public baseline never includes `deploy:*`. After create, only an **org admin** may change a sponsor's visibility in that org.
Lists groupable/filterable by platform, owner (AUTH-50), and associated teams of the viewer's org (§4.5.2).

SAVVI org admins can list and manage teams across all organizations (membership stays constrained to the team's own org, AUTH-6). SAVVI members see sponsor–team assignments across organizations (stories 23, 27–29).
